idiom_name: validating accessor properties (get) and a Proxy get trap
implementation_notes: No framework is needed: a get accessor runs the check when the property is read, and a Proxy whose get trap validates the target defers every check to the moment of use while leaving the stored payload untouched - the classic validator object collapses into a handler or a handful of accessors. Because the rule then runs per access rather than once, pair it with a memoised private field when the check is expensive, and keep a plain validator function when the caller must receive the complete list of field errors for a form. A validator object with composed rules is still justified for server-side payloads that several handlers share.
pitfalls: A getter that throws turns every incidental read into a failure: JSON.stringify, logging, spreading and devtools inspection all trigger it, so a validating accessor can break code paths that never intended to use the value.

Proxy invariants are enforced: a get trap that reports a different value for a non-configurable, non-writable target property throws a TypeError, so keep targets configurable or return the stored value.
Without memoisation the rule re-runs on every read, and a rule closing over mutable state can return different verdicts for the same property within one action.
